clue.text: Scotsman takes girl to see play

parts.note: Mac is a stock informal address for a Scotsman, from the common surname prefix
Beth is a girl's name, short for Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A Scottish man takes his girlfriend out to the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy about the Scottish king is one of the best-known plays in English.

clue.text: A Sheridan character, we hear, is coming

indicators.note: signals a word sounding like the phrase

parts.note: Sheridan's play The Rivals is full of rivals, so one of its characters is a rival

explanation.surface: Someone from an eighteenth-century play is about to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheridan wrote the comedy The Rivals, so any of its characters is a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun meaning the act of coming or reaching a place, so it fits 'coming' as a noun.

clue.text: Started, for instance, during Prohibition

indicators.note: during means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
e.g. abbreviates for example, i.e. for instance

explanation.surface: Something got going in America's dry era of the 1920s.
explanation.walkthrough: Prohibition with a capital suggests the US alcohol ban, but it is just BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Commenced or got under way is the past tense of begin.

clue.text: Collects cheats

definitions.meaning: to gather or receive, as when a hostess receives guests or ... washing

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both receiving or gathering things and deceiving someone, two distinct senses.

clue.text: Go ahead — make a loan

definitions.meaning: to lend money, often against future wages

explanation.surface: A lender tells a borrower to proceed with the loan.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for moving forward and for lending money upfront, two separate senses.

clue.text: Injury puts years on mother

indicators.note: on here means the years piece is tacked onto the end of the mother piece

parts.note: a dam is a mother, especially of animals
an age is a long span of years

explanation.surface: Getting hurt makes a mum look older.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm or hurt done to something is a close synonym of injury.

clue.text: Coming over a river, which may be exciting

indicators.note: in a down clue over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: an advent is a coming or arrival
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Crossing a river may provide a thrill.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a Yorkshire river, a common crossword stand-by.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertaking that may be thrilling or risky describes an adventure.

clue.text: Bound to be against punishment

parts.note: con is against, as in pros and cons
a fine is a monetary punishment

explanation.surface: Seems to say someone is sure to oppose penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to be' reads as 'certain to be', but 'Bound' is a verb meaning limit.
explanation.definitionFit: To bound something is to limit or restrict it, which means to confine.

clue.text: Upset, stand it no more — protest!

indicators.note: upset means the following words are overturned into new order

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry from someone who has had enough and wants to demonstrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A public march or rally against something is a protest.

clue.text: Key equipment in a sailing vessel

parts.note: B is a musical key
rig means gear or equipment, as in a drilling rig

explanation.surface: Essential gear aboard a sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' reads as 'essential' but gives the musical key B.
explanation.definitionFit: A brig is a two-masted square-rigged ship.

clue.text: Order one still refuses to obey

definitions.text: Order one still refuses to obey

parts.words: Order one still refuses to obey
parts.note: a policeman's command to loiterers to move along is one that anybody standing still is defying

explanation.surface: Someone who stays put is ignoring an instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' means motionless: a person standing still is precisely disobeying the command to move along.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the command police give to stop people loitering, so the stationary person defies it.

clue.text: They happen to upset Steven

indicators.note: upsetting the name Steven knocks its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Things that happen tend to distress poor Steven.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurrences or happenings are things that take place, so a plural noun fits 'they happen'.

clue.text: Fabric on instrument to perish

parts.note: an organ is a keyboard musical instrument
to perish is to die

explanation.surface: Cloth draped over a musical instrument is about to rot.
explanation.definitionFit: Organdie is a fine, stiff, translucent cotton muslin used for dresses.

clue.text: Warn head to display vigilance

parts.note: to alert someone is to warn them
a ness is a headland, a promontory, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Dungeness

explanation.surface: Cautioning the boss in order to show you are watchful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland here, not a boss: NESS is a word for one, found in place names such as Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Watchfulness and readiness for danger is a synonym of vigilance.

clue.text: Don't forget to get together again

explanation.definitionFit: The word means remember and, split as re-collect, means gather again.

clue.text: Still quite upset

indicators.note: upset means the word quite is knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone remains rather distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like 'even now' but is the definition: calm or silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Still as an adjective means calm, silent and without noise or movement.

clue.text: Spots, we hear, before the eyes?

indicators.note: signals that a word sounding the same as the synonym is wanted

parts.note: specks are small spots or flecks

explanation.surface: Seeing floaters or spots in front of your vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before the eyes?' is a playful definition: glasses sit in front of the eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacles, informally, are worn in front of the eyes; the question mark flags the whimsical description.

clue.text: Arranged Cup Final doesn't start — distressing

indicators.note: arranged means the remaining letters are put into a new order
the phrase loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: A rigged football final is upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't start' drops C from CUPFINAL, and 'Arranged' rearranges UPFINAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Causing pain or distress, so a painful scene is a distressing one.

clue.text: Wrong, or sure one is wrong

indicators.note: the closing word says these letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An insistence that a confident person can still be mistaken.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistaken or incorrect is the meaning of this adjective, matching wrong.

clue.text: Use suntan lotion? It can also help in the rain

definitions.meaning: split in two, the word suggests putting lotion on your body

definitions.text: It can also help in the rain
definitions.meaning: a waterproof coat of oiled cloth

explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it describes greasing up your body; as one word it is a waterproof garment.

clue.text: All by oneself, helpless?

explanation.definitionFit: The word means alone, without assistance, which is literally lacking help.

clue.text: A group of inspirational females entertains

parts.note: the Muses are the nine goddesses inspiring the arts

explanation.surface: A troupe of inspiring women puts on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Diverts or delights someone, a synonym of entertains as a third-person verb.

clue.text: Certificate goes to leading tactful envoy

parts.note: a diploma is a certificate of qualification

indicators.note: leading points to the first letter of the word tactful

explanation.surface: A qualified, tactful envoy is described by credentials and manners.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat is an official representative sent abroad, which is an envoy.

clue.text: All the difference between life and death?

indicators.note: making a difference to the words All the gives them a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A proverbial phrase about the vital gap between living and dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All the difference' is a stock phrase; here it means the letters of 'All the' are altered. The definition is whimsical: a fatal dose stands on the line between life and death.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deadly is what moves a person from living to dead, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Formidable opponent of note in a row

indicators.note: in means the note sits inside the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A fearsome rival with a famous name in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of note' looks like 'famous', and 'row' like a quarrel, but row is TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce, aggressive competitor is called this, after the big cat.

clue.text: Dessert wine may give one a further jolt

parts.note: afters is British informal for pudding or dessert
hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A sweet course with a glass of wine might give you a second surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British slang for the dessert course; HOCK is a British name for Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor following a main earthquake is a further jolt.

clue.text: They're very high in theatrical circles

definitions.text: They're very high in theatrical circles

parts.words: They're very high in theatrical circles
parts.note: the upper gallery of a theatre carries a nickname shared with deities, seated highest of all

explanation.surface: Seems to describe self-important stage people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circles' is also the tiered seating in a theatre; the top gallery is nicknamed after deities.
explanation.definitionFit: In British theatres the highest, cheapest gallery seats are traditionally called by this name.

clue.text: Government by the best? Have a wry smile about it

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the word it
wry means twisted, so the letters of smile are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A sardonic reaction to the idea of rule by the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wry' makes ELISM from the smile, and 'about' wraps that round the word it. The question mark admits the definition is loose: the doctrine favours an elite rather than being government itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The belief that a select, superior few should run things is a fair loose description of rule by the best.

clue.text: I'd turn awkward on a point and butt in

indicators.note: awkward indicates the words I'd turn are clumsily rearranged

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Someone's clumsy turn lets them push into a conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges IDTURN into INTRUD; E is east.
explanation.definitionFit: To interrupt or enter uninvited is to intrude.
